source.title: Hypothesis on Composition Circuits in Vision Transformers

record.file_problem: None; the full post text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The post proposes a hypothesis about composition circuits in vision transformers but does not test induction behavior or rely on it as a tool. Its described attention-pattern observation does not establish the proposed functionality.
record.gate_note: The author explicitly says the proposed heads' functionality is not known and experiments are for later. The post describes attention patterns from one image's forward pass, but does not test whether they implement induction-like behavior.
record.test_reason: The post proposes an analogy between induction circuits and hypothesized 'composition circuits' in ViTs. It runs no induction test: no repeated-sequence cases, no prefix-matching or copying score. The author says the proposed functionality is not known and experiments will come later. The only observation is a qualitative description of attention maps from one image, which does not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author hypothesizes that ViTs have 'composition circuits' analogous to induction circuits: a local 'modular attention head' followed by a composition head that gathers neighbouring patch features. The author offers this untested, citing only qualitative attention maps as suggestive.
record.recipe_differences: No reproduction method or experiment is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: In one forward pass of timm ViT-B/32, attention shifts from center-concentrated bands in early layers to more global patterns from about layer 8–9 onward.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ViT attention heads shift from local to global attention patterns with depth.

record.problems: The post is explicitly exploratory and reports no experiments validating the proposed circuit functionality. The attention-pattern observation is qualitative and based on one image's forward pass.

untested.parts: The ViT/vision-modality analogue is only hypothesized. No induction-like behaviour is measured in the ViT.

record.verdict_notes: Exploratory blog post with score 2. There are no quantitative results and no attempt to detect induction heads in the ViT.

versions.untested_parts: The post discusses a vision-transformer hypothesis but does not test for induction behavior across models, families, runs, or modalities.

rows.subject: timm/vit_base_patch32_224.augreg_in21k_ft_in1k
rows.operation_detail: Inspected attention-head patterns in a forward pass on one image.
rows.value: The author describes center-concentrated bands in early layers and more global information-sharing patterns from layer 8 or 9 onwards; the last 3-4 layers lack strong center bands.
rows.note: This is a qualitative description of attention maps; it does not test whether any head implements induction-like composition.
rows.check: Qualitative description of attention locality across layers in one ViT forward pass on one image. It does not measure induction behaviour ([A][B]…[A]→[B]) or composition with a previous-token head, so it bears on no version. The subject and condition are correct.
